examples.en: A mouse gnaws at the wall every night.

examples.ko: 강아지가 새 의자 다리를 갉고 있어요.
examples.en: The puppy is chewing on the leg of the new chair.

examples.ko: 토끼가 당근을 갉아 먹는 모습이 귀여워요.
examples.en: It is cute to see the rabbit nibbling on a carrot.
Insects ate the leaf and left holes in it.
I woke up to the sound of a mouse gnawing.
The squirrel nibbled on an acorn.

explain: '긁다'는 손이나 도구로 표면을 문지르는 거고, '갉다'는 이나 뾰족한 것으로 조금씩 뜯어내는 거예요. 보통 '갉아 먹다'로 많이 써요. 받침 ㄺ은 모음 앞에서 '갉아요[갈가요]'처럼 읽어요.

phrases.en: Small expenses eat away at my salary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻 그대로 이로 뜯어 먹는 것 말고, 돈이나 시간, 건강을 조금씩 줄어들게 한다는 비유로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Besides the literal meaning of gnawing, it is used figuratively for something slowly eating away at money, time or health.

explain_en: '긁다' means rubbing a surface with a hand or tool, while '갉다' means wearing something away bit by bit with teeth or a sharp edge. It is most often used as '갉아 먹다'. The final ㄺ is read as in '갉아요 [갈가요]' before a vowel.

examples.en: This cafe's interior is really stylish.
It's a stylish design, so it stands out.
I envy my friend who dresses with such good taste.
The photo is stylish and refined, so I like it.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 영상이 감각적이지만 이야기는 좀 어려워요.
examples.en: The film looks stylish, but the story is a bit hard to follow.

examples.ko: 감각적인 가게가 많아서 이 동네에 자주 와요.
examples.en: There are many stylish shops, so I often come to this neighborhood.

explain: 디자인, 옷, 영상처럼 취향이 좋고 세련된 것을 칭찬할 때 많이 써요. '센스 있다'와 비슷하지만 더 글 같은 느낌이에요. 보통 '감각적이다', '감각적인 + 명사' 형태로 쓰고, 이성이 아니라 느낌에 따른다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It is often used to praise things with good, refined taste, such as design, clothes or visuals. It is similar to '센스 있다' but sounds a little more written. It is usually used as '감각적이다' or '감각적인 + noun', and can also mean relying on feeling rather than reason.

examples.en: The pool lifeguard blew a whistle.
Ask the parking lot attendant for directions.
My father works as a forest fire watcher.

examples.ko: 감시원은 하루 종일 한 자리에 서 있어요.
examples.en: The watchman stands in one spot all day.

examples.ko: 해수욕장에서 감시원 아저씨가 위험하다고 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: At the beach, the lifeguard told us it was dangerous.
A notice went up saying they are hiring more watchers.

explain: '경비원'은 건물이나 구역을 지키는 사람이고, '감시원'은 수영장, 산불처럼 무언가를 살피는 역할 앞에 장소나 일을 붙여 '수영장 감시원'처럼 써요. 사람을 의심한다는 느낌보다 안전을 살피는 일이라는 느낌으로 많이 써요.
explain_en: '경비원' is a guard who protects a building or area, while '감시원' is someone whose job is to watch over something, with the place or task in front, as in '수영장 감시원'. It usually sounds like safety monitoring rather than suspicion.

examples.en: I wind the rope up from the well.
I slowly reeled in the fishing line.
If you roll up the blinds, the sunlight comes in.
I twisted my hair up and fixed it with a pin.
They wound up the anchor with a machine and the ship set off.
Be careful with your hands when you roll up the curtain.

explain: '감다'와 '올리다'가 합쳐진 말로, 줄이나 천을 돌려 감으면서 위로 올리는 동작이에요. 그냥 위로 올리면 '올리다', 줄을 당겨 올리면 '끌어올리다'를 쓰고, 감는 동작이 있을 때 '감아올리다'를 써요.
explain_en: It combines '감다' (to wind) and '올리다' (to raise), describing winding a rope or cloth while lifting it. If you just lift something, use '올리다', and if you pull it up, '끌어올리다'; use '감아올리다' when winding is involved.

en: seamless; as good as new; perfectly repaired

examples.en: I glued the broken plate and it looks like new.

examples.ko: 수리했는데 감쪽같아서 어디가 고장 났었는지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: It was repaired so seamlessly that I can't tell where it was broken.
He fooled his family completely.
After treatment at the hospital, the wound healed without a trace.
His skill was so flawless that everyone was amazed.

examples.ko: 얼룩이 하나도 안 보이네요. 정말 감쪽같네요.
examples.en: I can't see a single stain. It's really spotless.

explain: 흔적이 하나도 없이 깔끔하거나 아무도 눈치채지 못할 때 써요. 주로 '감쪽같이 속이다', '감쪽같이 사라지다'처럼 부사 '감쪽같이'로 많이 나와요. 수리나 변장 같은 좋은 일에도, 속임수 같은 나쁜 일에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes something that leaves no trace or that nobody notices. It mostly appears as the adverb '감쪽같이', as in '감쪽같이 속이다' or '감쪽같이 사라지다'. It can describe good things such as repairs and disguises, or bad things such as tricks.

examples.ko: 이 국물은 감칠맛이 나서 자꾸 생각나요.
examples.en: This broth has such a savory depth that I keep thinking about it.

examples.ko: 다시마를 넣으면 감칠맛을 더할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Adding kelp can give it more savory flavor.

examples.ko: 더덕구이가 감칠맛 있어서 밥 한 공기를 다 비웠어요.
examples.en: The grilled deodeok was so savory that I finished a whole bowl of rice.
It has a rich taste, but it's too salty.

examples.ko: 그 집 찌개의 감칠맛에 반해서 또 주문했어요.
examples.en: I fell for the savory taste of that place's stew and ordered again.
The savory taste is good and the aroma is good too.

explain: '맛있다'와 달리 입에 착 붙고 자꾸 당기는 깊은 맛을 말해요. 단맛, 짠맛, 신맛, 쓴맛과 함께 기본 맛으로 꼽는 맛(우마미)이고, 다시마나 멸치 육수, 버섯, 고기처럼 깊게 우러나는 맛에 많이 써요. 보통 '감칠맛이 나다', '감칠맛이 있다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '맛있다', it describes a deep, savory taste that makes you want more. It is counted as a basic taste alongside sweet, salty, sour and bitter (umami), and is often used for flavor from kelp or anchovy broth, mushrooms and meat. It is usually said as '감칠맛이 나다' or '감칠맛이 있다'.

examples.en: This year the number of customers doubled compared to last year.
I was surprised that prices went up by double.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 양이 다른 곳의 갑절이에요.
examples.en: This shop gives double the amount of other places.

examples.ko: 시험 때문에 평소보다 갑절은 더 열심히 공부했어요.
examples.en: Because of the exam, I studied twice as hard as usual.

examples.ko: 이번 달 전기 요금이 갑절 가까이 나왔어요.
examples.en: This month's electricity bill came out at nearly double.
Pour in more water until it doubles.

explain: '두 배'와 같은 말이에요. 일상에서는 '두 배'를 더 많이 쓰고, '갑절'은 말이나 글에서 조금 예스럽고 정겨운 느낌이 있어요. 세 배, 네 배에는 쓰지 않고 꼭 두 배일 때만 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '두 배' (twice as much). In daily life '두 배' is more common, and '갑절' sounds a little old-fashioned and warm. It is only for exactly double, not for three or four times.

en: be expensive; be valuable; be costly

examples.en: This painting is worth much more than I thought.
Don't put valuable items in your bag.
The ring my grandmother passed down was worth quite a lot.

examples.ko: 요즘 이 지역 땅은 값나가니까 팔기 아까워요.
examples.en: Land in this area is valuable these days, so it feels a shame to sell.

examples.ko: 값나갈 것 같아서 중고 가게에 가져가 봤어요.
examples.en: I thought it might be worth something, so I took it to a secondhand shop.

examples.ko: 예전에 값나가던 물건이 지금은 많이 싸졌어요.
examples.en: Things that used to be worth a lot have become much cheaper now.

explain: '비싸다'는 가격이 높다는 말이고, '값나가다'는 가치가 있어서 값이 꽤 나간다는 느낌으로 물건에 주로 써요. 보통 '값나가는 물건'처럼 꾸미는 형태로 많이 나와요.
explain_en: '비싸다' just says the price is high, while '값나가다' suggests an item is worth a good amount because of its value. It is mostly used for objects and often appears as a modifier, as in '값나가는 물건'.

examples.en: This stamp becomes more valuable as it gets older.
I want to spend a meaningful day.
It is important to spend money in a worthwhile way.
Volunteering is worthwhile and rewarding work.

examples.ko: 이 편지는 저한테 값있어서 오래 보관해요.
examples.en: This letter means a lot to me, so I keep it for a long time.
I bought it thinking it would be worth something.

explain: 가격이 높다는 뜻보다 '가치가 있다'는 느낌이 강해요. 일상 대화에서는 '값지다'를 더 자주 쓰고, '값있는 일/경험/시간'처럼 의미 있는 것에 많이 붙어요.
explain_en: It is less about a high price and more about having real worth. In daily talk '값지다' is more common, and '값있는' often goes with meaningful things such as work, experiences or time.

examples.ko: 고속도로에서 타이어가 터져서 갓길에 차를 세웠어요.
examples.en: A tire blew out on the highway, so I stopped the car on the shoulder.
You must not drive on the shoulder.
Driving on the shoulder is dangerous, so it is cracked down on.

examples.ko: 차가 고장 나서 갓길에서 견인차를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: My car broke down, so I waited for a tow truck on the shoulder.
I turned on the hazard lights and slowly drove to the shoulder.

examples.ko: 갓길은 급한 차가 설 때만 쓰는 곳이에요.
examples.en: The shoulder is only for emergencies.

explain: 고속도로나 자동차 전용 도로 가장자리에 비상시를 위해 만든 길이에요. 일반 도로의 길 가장자리는 보통 '길가'라고 해요. 평소에는 달리면 안 되고 고장이나 사고 때 차를 세우는 곳이에요.
explain_en: It is the strip at the edge of a highway or expressway made for emergencies. The edge of an ordinary road is usually called '길가'. You should not drive on it normally; it is for stopping when a car breaks down or in an accident.

examples.ko: 갓김치는 맛이 알싸해서 밥이랑 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: Mustard leaf kimchi has a sharp taste and goes well with rice.
I bought gatgimchi in Yeosu and brought it back.
The gatgimchi tastes better now that it has fermented.
Try wrapping meat in gatgimchi to eat.

examples.ko: 갓김치 한 통 보내 주셔서 감사해요.
examples.en: Thank you for sending me a tub of gatgimchi.
I like gatgimchi too.

explain: 갓으로 담근 김치로, 배추김치와 달리 톡 쏘고 알싸한 맛이 나요. 전라남도 여수의 갓김치가 유명해요. 익을수록 쓴맛이 줄고 맛이 깊어져요.
explain_en: It is kimchi made with mustard greens and, unlike cabbage kimchi, has a sharp, pungent taste. The gatgimchi from Yeosu in South Jeolla is famous. As it ferments, the bitterness fades and the flavor deepens.

examples.en: The newborn next door cries all night.

examples.ko: 갓난아이를 안을 때는 목을 받쳐 주세요.
examples.en: When you hold a newborn, support its neck.
Traveling with a newborn is not easy.
He fell fast asleep like a newborn baby.
They say breast milk is best for a newborn.

examples.ko: 우리 조카는 아직 갓난아이라서 하루 종일 자요.
examples.en: My nephew is still a newborn, so he sleeps all day.

explain: 태어난 지 얼마 안 된 아기를 말해요. 일상에서는 그냥 '아기'를 가장 많이 쓰고, '신생아'는 병원이나 뉴스처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 써요. '갓난애'는 줄여서 편하게 말할 때 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to a baby who was born very recently. In daily life '아기' is most common, and '신생아' is used in formal settings such as hospitals or news. '갓난애' is the shortened, more casual form.

examples.en: The newborn sleeps soundly in her mother's arms.
I was nervous because it was my first time holding a newborn.
I woke up to the sound of a baby crying.

examples.ko: 갓난애한테는 손을 깨끗이 씻고 만져야 해요.
examples.en: You should wash your hands before touching a newborn.
Only a newborn and the grandmother are in that house.
Our youngest has been gentle since he was a newborn.

explain: '갓난아이'를 줄인 말이라 말할 때 더 편하게 나와요. 글에서는 '갓난아이'가 더 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '아기'가 가장 흔해요. '갓'은 막 그렇게 됐다는 뜻이라 갓 태어난 아이라는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of '갓난아이', so it comes out more easily in speech. In writing '갓난아이' appears more often, and in daily talk '아기' is the most common. The '갓' part means just now, so it gives the sense of a freshly born child.

examples.en: I sat on the riverbank and fished.
The boat slowly approached the riverbank.
Walking along the riverbank feels refreshing.
Children play on the riverbank throwing pebbles.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 강기슭이 물에 잠겼어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot and the riverbank went under water.
Reeds grew thick along the riverbank.

explain: 강물과 땅이 닿는 가장자리를 말해요. 일상에서는 '강가'를 더 자주 쓰고, '강기슭'은 글이나 이야기에서 조금 더 풍경을 그리는 느낌이에요. 사람이 쌓은 '강둑'과는 달라요.
explain_en: It is the edge where river and land meet. In daily life '강가' is used more often, and '강기슭' sounds more scenic in writing and stories. It differs from '강둑', which is a built-up embankment.

examples.en: I eat rice with kidney beans mixed in.
The kidney beans sprouted, so I planted them in a pot.

examples.ko: 초등학교 때 강낭콩 키우기 숙제가 있었어요.
examples.en: In elementary school we had homework growing kidney beans.
Boiled kidney beans taste good in a salad.
I made soup with kidney beans.
Kidney beans are also rich in protein.

explain: 밥에 섞어 먹거나 수프, 샐러드에 넣는 콩이에요. 팥이나 완두콩과는 다른 콩이고, 학교에서 식물을 관찰할 때 키우는 콩으로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a bean eaten mixed into rice or added to soup and salad. It is different from red beans and green peas, and it often appears as the bean children grow when observing plants at school.

examples.en: I bought a bag of puffed corn at the market.
My grandmother popped corn for me.
The puffed corn is so nutty that I keep reaching for it.
Puffed corn is good as a snack.
The child shared the puffed corn and snacks.
They say people used to boil corn porridge in the old days.

explain: 옥수수를 정겹게 부르는 말이에요. 특히 튀긴 옥수수 과자를 가리킬 때 많이 써요. 영화관에서 먹는 '팝콘'과 비슷하지만, '강냉이'는 좀 더 전통 간식 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is a warm, familiar word for corn, and is especially used for popped or puffed corn snacks. It is similar to the '팝콘' you eat at the movies, but '강냉이' feels more like a traditional snack.

examples.en: Putting gangdoenjang on a wrap makes it taste great.
For lunch today I mixed rice with gangdoenjang.
Gangdoenjang has almost no broth.
The gangdoenjang my mom makes is the best.
Please tell me how to make gangdoenjang.

examples.ko: 밥과 강된장만 있어도 한 끼가 돼요.
examples.en: Rice and gangdoenjang alone make a meal.

explain: 된장찌개와 달리 물을 거의 넣지 않고 되직하게 졸인 된장 요리예요. 밥에 비비거나 쌈에 얹어 먹을 때 많이 써요. 국물을 떠먹는 요리가 아니라 곁들이는 반찬에 가까워요.
explain_en: Unlike doenjang-jjigae, it is a thick, reduced soybean paste dish made with almost no water. It is often mixed into rice or put on wraps. It is closer to a side dish than a soup you spoon up.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 강둑이 무너질까 걱정이에요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so I'm worried the embankment might collapse.
I run along the riverbank every evening.
The cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the embankment.
Children fly kites on top of the embankment.
It takes ten minutes by bike to get to the embankment.

examples.ko: 강둑은 물이 넘치지 않게 막아 줘요.
examples.en: The embankment keeps the water from overflowing.

explain: 강물이 넘치지 않게 흙이나 돌로 쌓은 둑이에요. 자연스러운 물가인 '강기슭'과 달리 쌓아 올린 언덕이라서, 위에 산책로나 자전거길이 있는 곳이 많아요.
explain_en: It is a bank built of earth or stone to keep a river from overflowing. Unlike '강기슭', the natural water's edge, it is a built-up ridge, and many have walking or bike paths on top.

examples.ko: 그 장면이 아직도 기억에 강렬히 남아요.
examples.en: That scene still remains vividly in my memory.
He intensely wanted to succeed.
It was an afternoon with the midsummer sun blazing down.

examples.ko: 그 노래의 멜로디가 강렬히 귀에 남았어요.
examples.en: The melody of that song stayed vividly in my ears.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 도와 달라고 강렬히 호소했어요.
examples.en: The child pleaded fervently for help.

examples.ko: 이 일을 꼭 하고 싶다는 생각이 강렬히 들었어요.
examples.en: I felt a strong urge to do this work.

explain: 감정, 바람, 인상, 햇빛이 아주 세게 느껴질 때 써요. '강하게'보다 글 같고 진지한 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '아주 강하게', '정말 세게'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is used when feelings, wishes, impressions or sunlight are felt very strongly. It sounds more written and serious than '강하게'. In everyday talk people often say '아주 강하게' or '정말 세게' instead.

examples.en: The river breeze is cool, so it's nice for a walk.
I rode my bike in the river breeze.
The river wind in winter is really biting.
My hair blew in the river wind.
Thanks to the river breeze, the heat eased a bit.
I came out to the Han River to get some fresh river air.

explain: 강 위나 강가에서 부는 바람이에요. 여름에는 시원하고 겨울에는 차갑게 느껴져요. '바닷바람', '산바람'처럼 장소 뒤에 '바람'을 붙인 말이고, '쐬다'와 잘 어울려서 '바람을 쐬다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the wind blowing over a river or along its banks, feeling cool in summer and cold in winter. It follows the pattern of '바닷바람' and '산바람', place plus '바람'. It pairs well with '쐬다', as in '바람을 쐬다'.

en: nerves of steel; a bold person

examples.ko: 저는 강심장이 아니라서 발표할 때 떨려요.
examples.en: I don't have strong nerves, so I get nervous when I present.

examples.ko: 혼자 귀신의 집에 들어가다니 정말 강심장이네요.
examples.en: Going into a haunted house alone, you're really fearless.
He has nerves of steel, so he didn't tremble even in the interview.

examples.ko: 강심장인 사람만 번지 점프를 할 수 있대요.
examples.en: They say only people with strong nerves can bungee jump.

examples.ko: 강심장을 가진 선수라서 마지막 순간에도 침착했어요.
examples.en: As a player with nerves of steel, he stayed calm even at the last moment.
You slept soundly the night before the exam? You have nerves of steel.

explain: 겁이 없고 담이 큰 사람을 말해요. 칭찬일 때도 있고, 놀랍다는 뜻으로 가볍게 말할 때도 있어요. 반대로 쉽게 겁먹고 긴장하는 사람은 '소심하다'나 '새가슴'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes someone who is fearless and bold. It can be praise, or a light remark of surprise. The opposite, someone who gets scared or nervous easily, is called '소심하다' or '새가슴'.

examples.en: It's bitterly cold this morning, so I layered up.
The cold snap continued and the water pipes froze.
People lined up even in the bitter cold.
My hands froze stiff in the bitter cold.
The cold snap will ease from tomorrow.
I brought hand warmers to beat the bitter cold.

explain: 눈은 안 오는데 매섭게 추운 날씨를 말할 때 주로 써요. 뉴스에서 쓰는 '한파'보다 일상 말이에요. '강추위가 몰아치다', '강추위가 계속되다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for weather that is fiercely cold without snow. It is more of an everyday word than the news term '한파'. Common phrases include '강추위가 몰아치다' and '강추위가 계속되다'.

examples.ko: 이번 주는 야근 강행군이라 너무 피곤해요.
examples.en: This week is a grind of overtime, so I'm exhausted.

examples.ko: 사흘 동안 강행군을 했더니 몸살이 났어요.
examples.en: After three days of nonstop pushing, I came down with aches.

examples.ko: 여행 일정이 강행군이어서 쉴 틈이 없었어요.
examples.en: The travel schedule was so packed that there was no time to rest.
After a punishing stretch of work, I finally finished the project.
During exam season, every day is a grind.

examples.ko: 강행군은 오래 하면 건강에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Pushing yourself nonstop for long is bad for your health.

explain: 일정이 빡빡해서 쉬지 못하고 계속 일하거나 움직이는 것을 말해요. 원래는 군대 행군에서 온 말이지만 일상에서는 여행, 일, 공부에 많이 써요. '강행군을 하다', '강행군이다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It describes working or moving nonstop on a packed schedule without rest. It comes from the idea of a forced military march, but in daily life it is used for trips, work and study. It is said as '강행군을 하다' or '강행군이다'.

examples.en: When it rained, the frogs croaked.

examples.ko: 밤새 개굴개굴 소리가 들려서 잠을 설쳤어요.
examples.en: I heard croaking all night and couldn't sleep well.
There's the sound of croaking from the pond.

examples.ko: 아이가 개구리 흉내를 내며 개굴개굴 했어요.
examples.en: The child imitated a frog and went ribbit ribbit.

examples.ko: 개굴개굴 하고 울던 소리가 갑자기 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The croaking sound suddenly stopped.
A croaking chorus began in the rice field.

explain: 개구리가 우는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 동요나 그림책에 자주 나오고, 보통 '개굴개굴 울다'처럼 '울다'와 함께 써요. 소리를 흉내 내는 말이라서 아이들과 이야기할 때 많이 들려요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound of a frog. It often appears in children's songs and picture books and usually goes with '울다', as in '개굴개굴 울다'. Because it imitates a sound, you hear it a lot when talking with children.

examples.ko: 초등학교 때 육 년 동안 개근상을 받았어요.
examples.en: I received a perfect attendance award for six years in elementary school.

examples.ko: 개근상은 일 년 동안 결석하지 않은 학생에게 줘요.
examples.en: The perfect attendance award goes to students who were never absent for a year.
The perfect attendance certificate is still in the drawer.

examples.ko: 한 번도 안 빠졌는데 개근상이 없어서 아쉬웠어요.
examples.en: I never missed a day, so it was a pity there was no award.

examples.ko: 개근상보다 성적이 더 중요하다고 생각하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people think grades matter more than a perfect attendance award.
A perfect attendance award is nice, but health comes first.

explain: '개근'은 결석 없이 다니는 것이고, '개근상'은 학교나 직장에서 그걸 칭찬하는 상이에요. 반대말은 '결석'이에요. 주로 학교 이야기에서 나오고, 옛날 사진이나 상장을 이야기할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: '개근' means attending without ever being absent, and '개근상' is the award for it at school or work. The opposite idea is '결석'. It mostly comes up when talking about school, often old photos or certificates.

examples.en: I had a weird, meaningless dream last night.
It's just a meaningless dream, so don't worry about it.
I dreamed of winning the lottery, but it was just a silly dream.
I've felt odd since this morning because of that silly dream.
This is the first time I've had such a nonsense dream.
It's probably a meaningless dream again. Don't worry.

explain: 앞뒤가 안 맞고 의미 없는 어수선한 꿈을 말해요. 좋은 일이나 나쁜 일을 알려 주는 꿈과 반대로, 아무 뜻이 없다고 말할 때 써요. '개꿈 꿨어'처럼 가볍게 말하는 구어예요.
explain_en: It refers to a jumbled, meaningless dream. It is the opposite of a dream that foretells something good or bad, and is used to say a dream means nothing. It is a casual spoken word, as in '개꿈 꿨어'.

examples.en: When spring comes, forsythia blooms yellow.
Please don't pick the forsythia.
Forsythia flowers are yellow, so they really stand out.

examples.ko: 개나리꽃과 진달래가 같이 핀 산길을 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked along a mountain path where forsythia and azaleas were blooming together.
I bought a dress as yellow as forsythia.
A bee landed on the forsythia flower.

explain: 그냥 '개나리'라고만 해도 꽃을 가리켜요. '개나리꽃'은 꽃 자체를 말할 때 써요. 봄을 알리는 노란 꽃으로 유명하고, 진달래와 함께 봄꽃으로 자주 같이 말해요.
explain_en: Just saying '개나리' can also refer to the flower; '개나리꽃' emphasizes the blossom itself. It is famous as a yellow flower that signals spring and is often mentioned together with azaleas as a spring flower.

examples.ko: 이번 주 개봉작 중에 볼 만한 게 있어요?
examples.en: Is there anything worth watching among this week's new releases?
Do you want to go to the theater this weekend to see a new release?

examples.ko: 이번 달 개봉작이 열 편이 넘어요.
examples.en: There are more than ten new releases this month.
Which new release are you looking forward to most?
Because it's a new release, the tickets sold out quickly.
This year's new releases were mostly fun.

explain: 극장에서 새로 개봉한 영화를 말해요. '신작'은 새로 나온 작품 전반을 말하고, '개봉작'은 극장에서 상영을 시작한 영화라는 점이 달라요. 주로 '이번 주 개봉작'처럼 시기를 붙여 써요.
explain_en: It means a movie newly released in theaters. '신작' covers any new work in general, while '개봉작' specifically refers to a film that has begun showing in cinemas. It is usually used with a time, as in '이번 주 개봉작'.

examples.en: That singer's voice is really distinctive.
Thanks to his distinctive outfit, he stood out.

examples.ko: 우리 반 친구들은 모두 개성적이고 재미있어요.
examples.en: All my classmates are unique and fun.
I like the room decorated with so much personality.

examples.ko: 너무 개성적이지 않은 디자인을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a design that isn't too unusual.
The more distinctive something is, the longer it stays in memory.

explain: '개성 있다'와 비슷하지만 '개성적이다', '개성적인 + 명사'로 쓰는 말이에요. 사람, 옷, 목소리, 디자인이 남들과 달라서 특색 있을 때 써요. 대체로 좋은 뜻이지만 너무 튀어서 부담스럽다는 느낌으로 쓸 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to '개성 있다' but is used as '개성적이다' or '개성적인 + noun'. It describes people, clothes, voices or designs that stand out as different. It is usually positive, but can also suggest something is so unusual that it feels like a lot.
